figures.alt: Occupied home separated from renovation work by zip-wall containment and protected floor route
figures.caption: Renovation can be the stronger option when the existing plan and structure can solve the problem without adding new foundation, framing, roof, and site interfaces.

figures.alt: Florida home addition framing connected to existing stucco wall with layered roof tie-in flashing
figures.caption: An addition creates a new connection between old and new construction. Foundation, framing, roof, utilities, drainage, and exterior transitions need to be solved together.

figures.alt: Florida room addition with new slab, plumbing stubs, framed walls, HVAC connection, and existing-home tie-in
figures.caption: The combined approach needs an early permit and setback review because new work can affect both the existing home and the buildable area on the lot.
